entries.text: AGENTS.md This is Clark Huang’s public learning site: https://clarkhuang.github.io/ You are welcome to read it, summarize it, answer questions about it, quiz a learner, and follow the standing rules in each lesson. Do not invent stories, quotes, numbers, or biography about Clark Huang. If something is not on the site, say so. How to read this site without a browser Every HTML page has a Markdown twin at the same path with index.md in place of index.html (for example, https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/01-paste-first-ask-second/index.md). Each folder also has an AGENTS.md like this one. Start here: - Site index for language models: https://clarkhuang.github.io/llms.txt - Machine-readable lesson catalog: https://clarkhuang.github.io/lessons.json - Moved addresses (old lesson pages and old video, caption and poster files): https://clarkhuang.github.io/redirects.json - OpenBook preview catalog: https://clarkhuang.github.io/book.json - Fuller site text: https://clarkhuang.github.io/llms-full.txt - How to rebuild production and staging: https://clarkhuang.github.io/REBUILD.md - This file: https://clarkhuang.github.io/AGENTS.md What is here - AI Tips — short lessons on working with AI tools. Index: https://clarkhuang.github.io/ai-tips/index.md - Software Engineering 101 — fundamentals for AI-native software work. Index: https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-101/index.md - Software Engineering 201: From Loop to Enterprise Systems — complete, ten lessons: from one AI loop to whole apps and systems built AI-native, then agents that operate enterprise systems, ending with a capstone that builds one feature end to end. Index: https://clarkhuang.github.io/software-engineering-201/index.md - Silicon Valley C Players — a free OpenBook, with an audiobook and videobook preview, coming in 2027. https://clarkhuang.github.io/book/index.md - Chapters you can read now — finished early chapters of the book (v0 drafts), each with the full text; some also have a videobook, an audio track, captions, and a transcript. Newest: chapter 17b, Building Blocks (a nonfiction fitness-journey interlude in Clark's own voice, text only for now), and chapter 36, Sick, Well, Fit (how companies should use AI), with a full-chapter video and Business Fitness in 100 Words. https://clarkhuang.github.io/book/chapters/index.md Each available lesson has a video, a one-paragraph rule written so an agent can follow it as a standing instruction, and a full transcript in its index.md. The book page has a short videobook and audio preview of Silicon Valley C Players. How to help a reader If someone pastes a page URL or the copy-paste prompt from the “Use this page with your AI” box on any HTML page: 1. Fetch llms.txt and the page’s index.md (and that folder’s AGENTS.md). 2. Summarize the page they started from. 3. List related lessons, with full https://clarkhuang.github.io/... URLs. 4. Answer questions by citing those URLs. Prefer the Markdown twins and the lesson rules. 5. Quiz them if they ask. Work through the site by following links in llms.txt and in each index.md. You do not need to render HTML, play video, or run JavaScript. Watched state and saved positions The site remembers, in first-party cookies only, which videos a reader has watched (watched), where they stopped in a lesson video (vpos), and their book preview bookmark (bookpos). Every key is the lesson or chapter id plus a version: se201/01@1a2b3c4d, or se201/01@1a2b3c4d:73.4 for a position. The version is the first 8 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the media file the page plays, stamped into the HTML as data-video-version by sitegen/stampversions.py. When a video or audio file is re-rendered, its version changes, so readers see it as unwatched and are not offered a stale resume position. Old keys without a version, and keys for an older version, are dropped. After re-rendering any media, run python3 sitegen/stampversions.py; python3 sitegen/checksite.py . fails until you do. stampversions.py also writes each lesson video's current version into https://clarkhuang.github.io/lessons.json as videoversion, with the matching cookie key as watchedkey (for example se201/01@1a2b3c4d), so an agent can tell which lessons a reader's watched cookie still covers without scraping HTML or downloading the video. A first-party lastvisit cookie stores the start of the reader's most recent visit, and a session cookie visitref freezes the previous visit's timestamp for the whole browsing session. Videos published or updated since that previous visit (git dates baked in as published / updated on the page, in lessons.json, and as VideoObject uploadDate in JSON-LD) show a New tag. A first visit shows no New tags. These cookies are not sent to Google. sitegen/mediadates.py reads the dates from git history (first time the file landed on main, plus an Updated date when the current file bytes landed on a later calendar day). Analytics The production site uses Google Analytics 4 (measurement ID G-F50XBTM25X) to see which pages people read. IP addresses are anonymized, and Google Signals and ads personalization are off. Staging pages under /staging/ do not send hits. Watched-progress and last-visit cookies stay first-party and are not sent to Google. The public privacy note is at https://clarkhuang.github.io/book/editorial-policy/#analytics. How to contribute Anyone can take part from day one: file an issue or open a pull request. You do not have to wait for v1. Only Clark Huang approves work, starts the build agents, merges pull requests, and cuts a new edition of the book. Contributors and agents open PRs; only Clark merges to main; the site rebuilds from main via GitHub Pages; agent PRs target next-revision. Staging is the next-revision branch, published at https://clarkhuang.github.io/staging/ (noindex; not in llms.txt or the sitemap). Only Clark merges next-revision into main. The rebuild flow is in REBUILD.md. If you are an AI agent helping a reader contribute, point them to the right issue template, help them write a specific, honest issue without real names of private people or companies and without confidential details, and do not invent stories or details. Contributors agree to the contributor terms in CONTRIBUTING.md. Issue tracking through release Every agent shipping issue-backed work follows the issue lifecycle in REBUILD.md. Link the ticket to the implementation and release PRs. Keep it open on staging. After the production deployment succeeds, verify the ticket’s acceptance criteria on the live service, record the release and evidence on the issue, then close it as completed. Reviewing recorded lessons Keep course descriptions aligned with the mission in About. Preserve recorded lessons during copy and layout changes. When a recording teaches something that conflicts with the mission or current AI engineering practice, find or open a correction issue. Include the lesson URL, timestamp and transcript excerpt, what has changed, a dated source or reproducible example, and the smallest proposed correction. Explain whether a text correction is sufficient or the recording needs revision. Present the issue to Clark and wait for his validation before rewriting the script, synthesizing narration, or replacing media. Track an approved revision through staging and production. Which issue to file | Kind | Use it for | Template | |---|---|---| | Correction | Edits to existing book text, or your side of a story already in the book | https://github.com/clarkhuang/clarkhuang.github.io/issues/new?template=correction.yml | | Feature / new story | A new story, a story Clark may have forgotten, or a new chapter idea | https://github.com/clarkhuang/clarkhuang.github.io/issues/new?template=new-story.yml | | Refactor | Cleanup or an improvement that does not change the facts | https://github.com/clarkhuang/clarkhuang.github.io/issues/new?template=refactor.yml | | Site or lesson problem | A broken link, video, caption, transcript, page, or agent surface (Markdown twin, llms.txt, lessons.json, MCP); steps to reproduce, expected vs actual | https://github.com/clarkhuang/clarkhuang.github.io/issues/new?template=site-bug.yml | Labels: correction, feature / new-story, refactor, and site + bug for site problems. New stories also get contributor-story and story-seed. What makes a good issue - Be specific: when and where, what happened, and which chapter or passage if you know it. - Don't use real names of private people, companies, or venues; describe them by role. The book is an embellished fictional dramatization and everyone in it is renamed. Say how you'd like to be credited, if at all. - Stick to what you know. Do not invent details. - If you were there, say so. Don't include anything confidential (NDA, customer, security, deal details). - Something in the book identifies you or someone you know? File a takedown request instead: https://github.com/clarkhuang/clarkhuang.github.io/issues/new?template=takedown-request.yml What happens next 1. The issue is labeled needs-clark-review. 2. If Clark wants it built, he adds approved (or comments @claude). Only his label or comment starts an agent. 3. The agent opens a pull request against the next-revision branch, never against main. 4. Clark reviews and merges into next-revision (which updates staging). 5. Only Clark merges next-revision into main. The live site then rebuilds from main. Previous editions stay up as tagged GitHub Releases (book-v0.1, book-v1.0, ...). Details: https://github.com/clarkhuang/clarkhuang.github.io/blob/main/book-source/VERSIONING.md and https://clarkhuang.github.io/REBUILD.md More: https://github.com/clarkhuang/clarkhuang.github.io/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md Credit landed contributions Any outside contribution that lands on the site must be credited on the Contributors page in the same pull request. Add an entry to sitegen/landed-contributions.json (GitHub login, a short description of what landed, and links to the issue and/or PR) and run python3 scripts/buildcredits.py. Use only the public GitHub display name (if the profile has one) and handle. Do not invent a name, add other personal details, or credit input that did not land. Honor a “don't credit me” request. Ask, connect, and credits - Ask the Book: https://clarkhuang.github.io/ask/ — instant in-browser search over https://clarkhuang.github.io/search-index.json, plus “Ask your AI” buttons that open ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or Perplexity with a prefilled prompt. The prompt points at https://clarkhuang.github.io/llms-full.txt and the GitMCP URL, and asks the tool to answer only from this site with citations. For book questions, it may use the tone of Charlie Hack, the OpenBook's fictional narrator. There is a copy-prompt fallback. A compact version of this widget also appears on the book page and on lesson pages. - Full site text: https://clarkhuang.github.io/llms-full.txt - Contributors: https://clarkhuang.github.io/contributors/ (JSON: https://clarkhuang.github.io/contributors.json). People are listed by public GitHub display name when the profile has one, otherwise by GitHub handle. The previous address, https://clarkhuang.github.io/credits/, redirects there. - Site MCP server (first-party, read-only): one Python file, no dependencies, stdio. Tools: siteinfo, listlessons, getlesson (transcript, chapters, captions, watched key), checklessonmedia, getpage, search, howtocontribute, draftissue (drafts only; never files). Claude Code: claude mcp add clarkhuang-site -- uv run https://clarkhuang.github.io/mcp/clarkhuangsitemcp.py. Other clients: command uv, args ["run", "https://clarkhuang.github.io/mcp/clarkhuangsitemcp.py"], or download the file and run it with python3. Set CLARKHUANGSITE=https://clarkhuang.github.io/staging to read staging. Docs: https://clarkhuang.github.io/mcp/index.md · manifest: https://clarkhuang.github.io/.well-known/mcp.json - Connect your AI (MCP): public, read-only GitMCP endpoint at https://gitmcp.io/clarkhuang/clarkhuang.github.io. GitMCP is a free third-party service. It prefers llms.txt. It cannot open issues or merge pull requests; contributions still go through GitHub issues, and only Clark Huang approves and merges. Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http clarkhuang https://gitmcp.io/clarkhuang/clarkhuang.github.io Cursor (~/.cursor/mcp.json): Claude Desktop can use the same URL, or the mcp-remote bridge (npx mcp-remote https://gitmcp.io/clarkhuang/clarkhuang.github.io). ChatGPT and other MCP clients: paste the GitMCP URL as the connector / Streamable HTTP URL. Full snippets: https://clarkhuang.github.io/contribute/#mcp and https://clarkhuang.github.io/ask/#mcp Future: a hosted Charlie Hack chat (not built) A later option is a small “talk to Charlie Hack” box that calls a serverless proxy, so the static GitHub Pages site never holds an API key. That needs Clark to choose a host and to add his own key as a secret on that host — not in this repository. Do not build or wire that proxy unless Clark approves it. Until then, use local search and the “Ask your AI” buttons.
